newsitem.title: CHINA: China state firms need more investors - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: China state firms need more investors - newspaper.

text.p: Chinese officials have urged an increase in individual investment in state-owned enterprises to revive the lumbering sector but have ruled out private ownership, the China Securities newspaper said on Monday.

"Share-holding reforms in state firms can adjust the national economic structure and strengthen the economy," the newspaper said, quoting Hong Hu, vice minister of the State Commission for Economic Restructuring.
"This is definitely not privatisation," Hu told a working conference about share-holding reforms in state enterprises.

China has struggled for years over how to tackle reform of its struggling state enterprises, held back by decades of Stalinist-style central planning and burdened with surplus labour they cannot shed and bad debt, without eroding state control.

In recent years, Beijing has increasingly allowed poorest performers to draw investment from the private or collective sector while maintaining that this does not mean the selling off the socialist family silver -- state firms -- to a new-rich class of private entrepreneurs.

However, Hu called for allowing and encouraging individuals to invest in state firms and for giving priority to the development of employee share-holding in through reforms. He gave no further details.
China is trying to turn most of its 110,000 state-run enterprises into limited holding companies to ease the burden on the government of subsidising loss-makers.

Beijing has promised that the share-holding firms will be independently managed and responsible for their own profits and losses. The government aims to retain ownership, although not to interfere in day-to-day administration.
By the end of 1996, 9,200 state-owned enterprises had completed the transition to become limited holding companies as part of the state reform plan, the Xinhua news agency said.
Total capital of the 9,200 firms was 600 billion yuan, with 43 percent held by the state, it said, adding that this showed the state was still the majority holder.
Among the limited holding companies, 107 firms were listed among China's top 500 industrial enterprises and 62 were in the top 500 service enterprises.
